3
A man of mass 75.2 kg uses a set of weighing scales to measure his mass three times. He
obtains the following readings.
mass / kg
reading 1
80.2
reading 2
80.1
reading 3
80.2
Which statement describes the precision and accuracy of the weighing scales?
A
not precise to  0.1 kg and accurate to  0.1 kg
B
not precise to  0.1 kg and not accurate to  0.1 kg
C
precise to  0.1 kg and accurate to  0.1 kg
D
precise to  0.1 kg and not accurate to  0.1 kg

hints: Notice the spread of the three scale readings 80.2, 80.1 and 80.2 kg and compare the largest difference to $0.1 \text{ kg}$.
Recall that precision means repeatability of the readings, while accuracy means closeness of the readings to the true mass of $75.2 \text{ kg}$.
Calculate $80.2 - 75.2$ in kg to test accuracy to $\pm 0.1 \text{ kg}$, and check if the $0.1 \text{ kg}$ spread supports precision.
walkthrough: Identify the true value $75.2 \text{ kg}$ and the three measured values $80.2 \text{ kg}$, $80.1 \text{ kg}$ and $80.2 \text{ kg}$.
Test precision by repeatability: maximum difference is $80.2 - 80.1 = 0.1 \text{ kg}$, so repeated readings agree within $\pm 0.1 \text{ kg}$.
Test accuracy by closeness to truth: typical error is $80.2 - 75.2 = 5.0 \text{ kg}$, which is much larger than $0.1 \text{ kg}$.
Conclude the scales show a systematic shift of about $5.0 \text{ kg}$ high: good repeatability but poor closeness to the true mass.
Therefore the scales are precise to $\pm 0.1 \text{ kg}$ and not accurate to $\pm 0.1 \text{ kg}$. This is option D

A.explanation: The spread of 80.2, 80.1, 80.2 kg is only $0.1 \text{ kg}$, so the scales are precise, and the $5.0 \text{ kg}$ shift from $75.2 \text{ kg}$ means they are not accurate.

B.explanation: The three readings agree to within $0.1 \text{ kg}$, so precision to $\pm 0.1 \text{ kg}$ is present even though accuracy is not.

C.explanation: Repeatability is good, but readings near $80.2 \text{ kg}$ are about $5.0 \text{ kg}$ above the true $75.2 \text{ kg}$, so accuracy to $\pm 0.1 \text{ kg}$ fails.

D.explanation: Readings differ by at most $0.1 \text{ kg}$, showing precision, but all are about $5.0 \text{ kg}$ high, showing a systematic error and poor accuracy.
